findings.reason: a node dispatched on §15 confirms the defect before repairing it, and cannot do so against an id that resolves to no run; the id or the anchor must be corrected first.
findings.text: §15 cites `power_convertor run r-20261028T112435754554-csrr-fdu-idm-stray-per-circuit` as the reproduction, but no run record with that id exists: `ls .../docs/state/power_convertor/runs/ | grep 20261028T112435754554` returns nothing, `grep -rl 112435754554` over the whole power_convertor tree returns nothing, and the nearest real run is `r-20261028T200825823020-csrr-fdu-stray-per-circuit` (node without `-idm`, dispatched 20:10Z, gate passed), so the only reproduction the section offers cannot be opened

findings.reason: the section's defect statement is its justification for the liveness clause, and a node checking it at the cited anchor finds a different wait; the plan should point at the artifact that holds the observed stall (the live pointer reading, or a pasted `crew view live` row) instead of a run whose manifest contradicts it.
findings.text: §6 says the run "wrote `status: waiting` with a `wc -l` probe on a rows file and a terminal value of 66" and read as working for 15 hours, but the run it cites (`r-20261029T040536910067-csrr-disruption-fdu-cases`, dispatched 2026-10-29T04:07Z) has a durable manifest at `.../crew/runs/r-20261029T040536910067-csrr-disruption-fdu-cases/manifest.md` whose `wait_probe` is `["grep","-ho","^EXIT=.*", ".../gate-rerun.log"]`, whose `wait_terminal` is `EXIT=0`, and whose `status` reads `complete`; the `wc -l`/66 wait and the `process_alive false` reading the section rests on are preserved in no artifact the section names

findings.reason: the arm cannot be made to fail or pass as written, so the node must either invent a reader outside its declared scope or drop the clause; naming `fleet_node`'s query (or reducing the clause to the process tree) changes the write paths and the arm.
findings.text: §6's deliverable makes "the run names no external job whose liveness the classifier can read as still alive" a clause of the classification, and the done-when's third arm requires "a waiting run … whose named external job is alive, stays waiting", but no job-liveness reader is named and none exists on the path the section extends: `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py` exposes `process_alive`/`_live_descendant` over pids only, and the sole job reader in the package is `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:357` (`squeue -h -j`), which is not in the write paths and is not named

findings.reason: an implementer must settle an unspecified ordering (and can pick one that sends the request to a metered lane the lead did not intend), so the section should name the order source explicitly.
findings.text: §15's remedy "chooses the first backend in the project's configured lane order that fits" names an ordering configuration that does not exist: the project's `docs/state/power_convertor/flight.yaml` declares only `review_excluded_backends` and `fences`, `reckon/_flight_schema.py` has no lane-order field, and `grep -rn "lane_order|backend_order|ordered_lanes" reckon/crew/*.py` finds only a docstring in `metering.py`, so the order is whatever the host `backends:` YAML mapping happens to emit

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §15's cited reproduction run resolves nowhere in the power_convertor tree.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's third arm requires a named external job to read as alive, and no such liveness reader is named in the section or present in the classifier it extends.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15's gate is a new test file at its declared path and §6's gate likewise; neither routes a log to a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `WAIT_PRODUCER_GONE_SECONDS`, `wait_probe_history` and the `context-fit` reason name mechanisms and outcomes, with no plan labels or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's cited run does not carry the wait declaration the section describes, and §15's "configured lane order" names no ordering that is configured anywhere.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 is one deliverable (never resolve a fallback route onto a lane that cannot hold the request); §6 is one deliverable (classify a producer-gone wait and raise one obligation).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §14's new `depends-on` (s11, s12) matches what it extends and repairs; §15 declares no upstream it actually consumes, and §6's classification is self-contained.
